results.title: Israel: opposition supporters celebrate narrow lead in exit polls
results.content: Supporters of Gadi Eisenkot celebrated in Tel Aviv as exit polls gave Israel's opposition bloc a narrow lead over Benjamin Netanyahu's camp, but no outright parliamentary majority.

results.title: Portugal: Lisbon housing crisis sparks protest outside parliament
results.content: Demonstrators gathered outside Portugal's parliament to protest against the housing crisis and police violence during recent camp clearances. The president has called for dialogue while defending police actions.

results.title: Mbappe apologises for Mao Zedong comment after Chinese sponsors drop him
results.content: Football superstar Kylian Mbappé has apologised after a video appearing to show him joking about Chinese leader Mao Zedong sparked outrage in China.

results.title: South Africa claims 7.6 kilometer-long freight train is the longest ever
results.content: A government-run company in South Africa claims that it has sent the longest freight train ever on a test run.

results.title: Botanists comb Gabon's rich rainforests with nature on the line
results.content: Each year, Gabon's lush rainforests yield the discovery of previously unknown plant species to botanists like Archange Boupoya, who believes that this exceptional yet largely mysterious natural wealth needs cataloguing to save.

results.title: Nigeria jail conditions blamed for deaths of 33 miners
results.content: Poor jail conditions led to the deaths of 33 young miners arrested on suspicion of illegal gold mining in central Nigeria, investigators said Tuesday, describing their treatment as “cruel and inhuman.”

results.title: South Africa: Athlete traverses 600 monkey bars under a 216-metre bridge
results.content: Suspended beneath South Africa's 216-metre-high Bloukrans Bridge, Thomas van Tonder crossed 600 monkey bars over more than 280 metres, completing the challenge in 47 minutes and 37 seconds.

results.title: Myanmar: spectacular lantern festival lights up ancient temples in Bagan
results.content: Hundreds of glowing lanterns floated into the night sky above Bagan's ancient pagodas. Thousands gathered to celebrate Thadingyut, Myanmar's Festival of Lights marking the end of Buddhist Lent.

results.title: DRC's former leader Kabila is Rwandan 'proxy,' Tshisekedi tells lawmakers
results.content: DR Congo's former president, Joseph Kabila, is a Rwandan stooge, his successor Felix Tshisekedi told lawmakers on Tuesday. Kabila this month joined forces with the Kigali-backed M23 armed group that's been leading an insurgency in eastern DRC for more than a decade.

results.title: Kylian Mbappé faces China backlash as major brands cut ties over Mao meme controversy
results.content: Football superstar Kylian Mbappé is a familiar face across China but that could soon change. The Real Madrid forward has reportedly been dropped by two major Chinese brands after a video circulated online in which he appeared to joke about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

results.title: Egypt detains journalist Lina Attalah after court ruling
results.content: Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah, editor-in-chief of the country's leading independent news outlet Mada Masr, was detained by security forces after being fined in a swift trial on Tuesday, the publication said.

results.title: How the Svalbard seed vault could help protect Africa's food future
results.content: Frozen in the Arctic: How the Svalbard seed vault could help protect Africa's food future

results.title: Benin fashion show takes inspiration from the seabed
results.content: A fashion show on the shores of Lake Toho in Ouidah to unveil 16 new indigo patterns inspired by the ocean.

results.title: NASA astronaut Christina Koch on life in space, humanity and her African connection
results.content: In an exclusive interview with Africanews on the sidelines of the ceremony, Koch reflected on how seeing Earth from space changed her perspective on humanity, global cooperation and the importance of diversity in exploration.

results.title: Tanzania's jailed opposition leader Tundu Lissu begins hunger strike
results.content: Tanzania's jailed opposition leader Tundu Lissu has begun a hunger strike in protest at his inability to access his lawyers. The Chadema party leader began refusing food on Monday after his legal team was barred entry to Ukonga prison, where he's being held.

results.title: Israelis vote in pivotal election as Netanyahu faces challenge from Eisenkot
results.content: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cast his ballot in Jerusalem, urging Israelis to vote “the right way” in a pivotal election.

results.title: Qatar sends 15 buses to Senegal ahead of Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics
results.content: With just days to go before the start of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, 15 buses gifted by Qatar arrived in the Senegalese capital. They're part of a Qatari initiative to support nations hosting international sporting events.

results.title: Ethiopia: At least 60 Christians killed in attacks in Oromia region
results.content: Religious authorities said all the victims were Christians but provided no further details about those responsible for the attacks.

results.title: Turkey: tornado kills at least four workers at Antalya construction site
results.content: At least four workers died when a tornado struck a construction site in Antalya, overturning accommodation cabins and a tower crane. Heavy rain also flooded roads in Istanbul.

results.title: IOC president arrives in Senegal ahead of the Youth Olympic Games
results.content: Zimbabwean Kirsty Coventry was welcomed by volunteers as Dakar prepares to host the first Olympic event in Africa.

results.title: Ukraine: firefighters battle flames and rescue dog from Kyiv ruins
results.content: A Russian missile and drone attack on Kyiv killed one person and injured 15. Emergency workers rescued a dog from the rubble, while strikes damaged university buildings and a major bridge.

results.title: University students in The Gambia protest over poor campus conditions
results.content: Hundreds of students in Gambia's capital Banjul demonstrated on Monday against poor conditions at the nation's leading university. Echoing demands by students across Europe, the University of The Gambia's student union called for a mass mobilisation, but urged participants to remain peaceful.

results.title: Niger accuses Chad of deadly drone attack in which two civilians died
results.content: The military authorities say they have summoned the Chadian ambassador over the incident and are demanding compensation for the damage caused.

results.title: Israel: October 7 families remember victims as voters head to polls
results.content: In Tel Aviv, families affected by the 7 October 2023 attacks observed a moment of silence as polling stations were opening across Israel for the general election.

results.title: Harry Kane become first English footballer to win Ballon d'Or in 25 years
results.content: He is the first English player in 25 years to win the sport's most presitigious individual prize, beating Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal.

results.title: South African ambassador calls for talks to ease tensions with US
results.content: Roelf Meyer said Pretoria is seeking "direct dialogue" with Washington as it seeks to avoid exclusion from a key US-Africa trade deal.

results.title: France: crowds fill Marseille's Old Port in anti-racism protest
results.content: Hundreds of people gathered at Marseille's Vieux-Port on Monday evening to protest against racism following a deadly shooting near Paris. Police estimated the crowd at 800, while organisers put attendance at more than 1,000.

results.title: Human rights activists condemn alleged abduction of Tanzanian govt critic
results.content: Human rights activists condemn the alleged abduction of Tanzanian dissident and former opposition official, Twaha Mwaipaya, in Kenya. results.title: Moscow prepares to host African leaders for Russia-Africa Summit
results.content: African leaders are gathering in Moscow for a series of high-level meetings focused on strengthening ties with Russia and shaping the future of global energy cooperation.

results.title: Sudan: Soaring prices worsen food crisis [ Africanews Today]
results.content: Torn apart by war, Sudan is grappling with the consequences of the armed conflict on its economy and its people. In Omdurman, bread supplies are dwindling, and residents can no longer afford to buy it.
